newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium sees progress on French Dassault case.
newsitem.headline: Belgium sees progress on French Dassault case.

text.p: Belgium's justice minister said on Thursday Belgium was closer to receiving information from France on allegations that French defence firm Dassault bribed Belgian political parties to secure a defence contract.

Replying to a parliamentary question Stefaan De Clerck said Belgian officials would be in touch with their French counterparts next week to discuss a solution to the issue of missing papers which dates back to January.

The issue caused tension between the two countries, raising fears in Belgium that France was stalling in the hope that the case which relates to a 1989 contract would reach the statute of limitations and would have to be dropped.

De Clerck said in his reply that his French counterpart Jacques Toubon had told him in April that 11 documents could not be handed over to the Belgian authorities in the interest of France's national defence.

De Clerck then proposed to Toubon to handle the documents in such a way that French interests would not be harmed and the Belgian judicial authorities would get the necessary information. He gave no details.
Contacts between the two ministries had now led De Clerck to believe that "the suggestion made could be acceptable to the French authorities," he said in his reply.
Police are investigating claims that Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) in kickbacks to parties to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian F-16 jets.

After months of lying dormant the "Dassault affair" sprang to life at the start of the year and even threatenend the stability of Belgium's centre-left government when top francophone socialist party officials were arrested on corruption charges in connection with the investigation.

A Belgian court last year issued an international arrest warrant for Serge Dassault, the group's founder and chairman, who has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions.
